subject.title: Control UI: Config upgrade/hardening suggestions should apply changes automatically with before/after diff and user acceptance, not direct users to edit files manually

question: Should Control UI recommendation cards be allowed to apply protected auth/security config changes such as `gateway.controlUi.allowInsecureAuth`, and what approval/audit policy must gate those writes?
rationale: The UI already has generic config diff and write primitives, but this request crosses a security-sensitive browser-to-Gateway config boundary where current policy deliberately protects auth-related paths.

options.title: Design protected recommendation flow
options.body: Create a narrow policy for which Control UI recommendations can propose config patches, require exact before/after diff acceptance, bind the base hash, and log/audit auth-related writes.

options.title: Limit to low-risk suggestions
options.body: Allow one-click apply only for non-protected recommendation paths and keep auth/security recommendations as manual guidance until the broader protected-config approval protocol lands.

options.title: Fold into protected-config approval
options.body: Treat this as UI-specific follow-through for https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/77886 if maintainers want one shared approval mechanism across agents and Control UI.

recommendation.title: Design protected recommendation flow
recommendation.body: Create a narrow policy for which Control UI recommendations can propose config patches, require exact before/after diff acceptance, bind the base hash, and log/audit auth-related writes.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved choice is a product/security boundary decision, and history points to steipete as the strongest routing owner across config safety and gateway-tool policy surfaces.
